format: html

# Simulating Dataset

```{r}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
```


```{r}
# Define parameters
beta_0 <- 2
beta_1 <- 0.2
sigma <- 4
```

## Simulate Predictor Variable

```{r}
# Generate random values
sun <- runif(n = 30, min = 0, max = 60)
```

## Calculate the expected value of the response

```{r}
# Calculate the _expected_ value of the response
exp_pg <- beta_0 + beta_1 * sun
```

## Simulate response variable

```{r}
# Simulate response variable
plant_growth <- rnorm(
  n = 30,
  mean = mean(exp_pg),
  sd = sigma
)
```

```{r}
# Visualize
plant_df <- tibble(Sun = sun,
        Plant_Growth = plant_growth)

ggplot(plant_df, aes(x = Sun, y = Plant_Growth)) +
    geom_point() +
    labs(title = "Title")
```

# Fit the model

```{r}
# Create lm model
plant_lm <- lm(Plant_Growth ~ Sun, data = plant_df)
```

```{r}
summary(plant_lm)
sigma(plant_lm)
```

# Interpret the model

## Increase sigma


```{r}
# Keep your predictor variable the same, but increase sigma by 2x
double_sigma <- sigma * 2
# Modify the following lines of code to re-run your simulation with the bigger sigma
expected_response2 <- beta_0 + beta_1 * sun
response_variable2 <- rnorm(
  n = 30,
  mean = mean(expected_response2),
  sd = double_sigma
)
plant_df2 <- tibble(Sun = sun, Plant_Growth = response_variable2)
model2 <- lm(Plant_Growth ~ Sun, data = plant_df2)

# Get your betas and their standard errors
summary(model2)
sigma(model2)
# How do they compare to the population parameters, relative to the original simulation?
```

## Increase n


```{r}
# Now increase n by 2x. You'll need to create more predictor variable values.
# Generate random values
sun3 <- runif(n = 60, min = 0, max = 60)

# Modify the following lines of code to re-run your simulation with the bigger n
expected_response3 <- beta_0 + beta_1 * sun3 #?
response_variable3 <- rnorm(
  n = 60,
  mean = mean(expected_response3),
  sd = sigma
)

plant_df3 <- tibble(Sun = sun3, Plant_Growth = response_variable3)

model3 <- lm(Plant_Growth ~ Sun, data = plant_df3)

# Get your betas and their standard errors
summary(model3)
sigma(model3)
# How do they compare to the population parameters, relative to the original simulation?
```
